## alphaXiv
alphaXiv provides access to a database of over 2.5 million academic research papers from arXiv. (computer science, mathematics, physics, statistics, quantitative biology/finance, electrical engineering, NOT biomedical, clinical, or life science papers from PubMed, Cell, Nature) These tools are useful when the user asks about, references, or discusses academic papers, scientific research, scholarly literature, citations, research topics, or anything related to academic work. If the user mentions a research area, methodology, scientific concept, asks for literature reviews, wants to find related work, or asks questions that could benefit from academic sources, consider using the search tools. When the user references a specific paper or asks about its content, the paper content and PDF query tools can help. Prefer searching for and citing real papers over relying on memory alone for research questions. The library tools manage the user's own folders of bookmarked papers: a paper can live in several folders at once, and 'to read', 'reading', and 'completed' are just the default folders rather than exclusive states. The researcher tools answer questions about people: who works on a subject, an organization's roster, where someone is now, who they publish with, and the user's own follows. Results address papers as [ID=<id>] and researchers as [SLUG=<slug>]; pass those values back to the tools that take a paper id or a researcher slug, and render them as https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/<id> and https://www.alphaxiv.org/@<slug> rather than showing the bracketed handle to the user.

## Anthropic_Economic_Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null means the value
  is not published for this cell; it may be zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Firecrawl
Firecrawl provides web, developer, and research search. Use firecrawl_search to find relevant results across the web and specialized indexes. For a programming question, firecrawl_developer_search searches indexed repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and curated documentation sites and returns the matched passages, and skills: "only" narrows it to agent-skill files; firecrawl_search with categories: ["developer"] reaches the same index beside ordinary web results, returning the hits in the web group rather than as passages and offering no skills filter. For a biomedical, life-science, clinical, or arXiv literature question, the firecrawl_research_* tools search the paper index, while categories: ["research"] on firecrawl_search filters ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites. Use the firecrawl_research_* tools to search academic and research literature, expand from anchor papers via the citation graph, and read full-text passages from a specific paper. All tools are read-only and return ranked results.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Gmail
This is an MCP server provided by Gmail API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Gmail.

## Google_Drive
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

## Hugging_Face
Hugging Face Hub MCP server for models, datasets, Spaces, collections, papers, and docs.
Prefer this connector's live Hub capabilities over the public website for all configured listings such as today's trending models, the current model leaderboard, daily papers, and paper popularity.

Use hf_fs for Hub filesystem and discovery:
- trending models: ls hf://models/trending
- trending datasets or Spaces: ls hf://datasets/trending, ls hf://spaces/trending
- trending papers / daily papers / paper of the day: ls hf://papers/trending, ls hf://papers/daily/latest
- search models, datasets, Spaces, collections, papers, or docs: search hf://models QUERY
- read a known file: cat hf://models/OWNER/NAME/README.md

Other advertised Hub tools can search or inspect a known repo id. Use hf_whoami for the current Hugging Face account.

hf:// URIs can be converted to browser URLs by replacing hf://buckets/OWNER/NAME/PATH with https://huggingface.co/buckets/OWNER/NAME/resolve/PATH; for models, datasets, and spaces, use https://huggingface.co[/datasets|/spaces]/OWNER/NAME/resolve/main/PATH. URL-encode each path segment.

arXiv paper ids (for example 2502.16161) are often used as references between datasets, models, and papers. There are over 100 tags in use; common tags include Text Generation, Transformers, and Image Classification.
Hugging Face tools are being used by authenticated user 'LBJLincoln26'

## Supabase
Here are guidelines for using Supabase tools effectively:

- Before making schema changes, inspect the existing tables so you understand the current structure
- When debugging issues, start by reading the project's logs and its security and performance advisories before making changes
- Look up the project's API URL and its publishable API keys when helping users configure client-side integrations
- SQL runs on the project's database server. Never read server-side files or run OS commands via SQL.

If you have access to a local development environment with a filesystem and shell:
- Install the Supabase agent skill for critical development and security guidance: `npx skills add supabase/agent-skills` (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/ai-skills.md)
- Use the Supabase CLI (`supabase`) for local development workflows such as starting a local stack, managing migrations, and running edge functions locally (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development.md)
- Prefer local development and testing before applying changes to a remote project

If you are running in a web-only or remote environment without filesystem or shell access:
- Rely on the MCP tools directly for all Supabase interactions
- Apply schema migrations carefully, as changes go directly to the remote project

## Vercel
Use the available Vercel tools and their input schemas. Discover the intended team and project before choosing resource IDs.

Reuse team, project, and deployment IDs supplied by the user or returned by tools. When scope is unknown, discover teams, then projects in the selected team. Ask only if the intended target remains ambiguous. Respect a project-scoped connection; do not guess combinations of IDs.

For troubleshooting, inspect the relevant deployment state, build output, or runtime logs before changing configuration. Use documentation search when platform behavior is unclear.

Filter reads to the relevant project, time range, and fields supported by the operation. Follow pagination when a complete list is needed; state when results are partial or truncated. Batch independent calls; wait for results before making dependent calls.

Inspect the target before modifying an existing resource when a read is available, and verify the resulting state afterward. For purchases, follow get_purchase_quote and the dedicated confirmation tool. Never decrypt environment values unless explicitly requested.

Inspect each call result, including failures within a batch. Correct invalid inputs from the returned schema. For access or not-found errors, verify scope instead of repeating guessed IDs; do not assume every not-found error means no access. Retry transient failures only when safe, and check state before retrying a write with an uncertain outcome. Distinguish accepted or pending work from completed work.

- Apply schema migrations carefully, as changes go directly to the remote project

## Vercel
Use the available Vercel tools and their input schemas. Discover the intended team and project before choosing resource IDs.

Reuse team, project, and deployment IDs supplied by the user or returned by tools. When scope is unknown, discover teams, then projects in the selected team. Ask only if the intended target remains ambiguous. Respect a project-scoped connection; do not guess combinations of IDs.

For troubleshooting, inspect the relevant deployment state, build output, or runtime logs before changing configuration. Use documentation search when platform behavior is unclear.

Filter reads to the relevant project, time range, and fields supported by the operation. Follow pagination when a complete list is needed; state when results are partial or truncated. Batch independent calls; wait for results before making dependent calls.

Inspect the target before modifying an existing resource when a read is available, and verify the resulting state afterward. For purchases, follow get_purchase_quote and the dedicated confirmation tool. Never decrypt environment values unless explicitly requested.

Inspect each call result, including failures within a batch. Correct invalid inputs from the returned schema. For access or not-found errors, verify scope instead of repeating guessed IDs; do not assume every not-found error means no access. Retry transient failures only when safe, and check state before retrying a write with an uncertain outcome. Distinguish accepted or pending work from completed work.

1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-command-deck
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	The Command Deck is the customer-facing front end of the Daliesk agent enterprise: 147 defined agents, the workflows between them, the live activity of a harness run, and a code-safety review placed on the target repository's own code.
6	
7	It is a Next.js 14 application (App Router, React 18) whose three scenes are three.js through `@react-three/fiber`. It reads one HTTP feed and, when that feed does not answer, replays the fixtures committed beside it — so the deck is fully usable, and demonstrable, with no server running and no API key.
8	
9	## Run it
10	
11	Run the first from the repository root; the second is `pnpm --dir apps/command-deck dev` under another name.
12	
13	```sh
14	pnpm install
15	pnpm run deck
16	```
17	
18	The deck serves on `http://localhost:3000`. Point it at a live feed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEED_URL`; the default is `http://localhost:4711`.
19	
20	The second line is the production build and the server over it; the third regenerates `fixtures/`.
21	
22	```sh
23	NEXT_PUBLIC_FEED_URL=http://localhost:4711 pnpm run deck
24	pnpm --dir apps/command-deck build && pnpm --dir apps/command-deck start
25	pnpm --dir apps/command-deck fixtures
26	```
27	
28	## The three views
29	
30	| Key | View | What it shows |
31	| --- | --- | --- |
32	| `1` | **Enterprise** (`/`) | Every defined agent as a node, clustered by division, edges for the delegations, verifications and judgements between them. A node pulses while its agent acts; a ring bursts where a certificate is issued. Clicking one opens its role, model route, preset, skills, tools, source file, and its own events in the run being followed. |
33	| `2` | **Process** (`/process`) | The program pipeline — departments, Verification, Judging, Integration — with every logged event travelling as a comet from its stage to the next. A timeline scrubber replays the run from any point; `Head` returns to live. |
34	| `3` | **Code safety** (`/safety`) | The reviewed repository as a code city: directories are districts, files are blocks scaled by size and coloured by language, and every finding is a marker standing on the line of code that carries it. The panel holds the findings table with severity, department and CWE filters, the certificate with its counts and its unverified list, the bilingual report, downloads, and the form that starts a new review. |
35	
36	`Esc` clears the selection. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` turns off the auto-orbit, the pulsing and the chromatic aberration, and holds bloom at a constant intensity.
37	
38	![The enterprise view: 147 agents in ten division clusters](docs/enterprise.png)
39	
40	![The process view: departments, verification, judging and integration](docs/process.png)
41	
42	![The code-safety view: the code city with findings on their files](docs/safety.png)
43	
44	## The feed contract
45	
46	The deck reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEED_URL` (default `http://localhost:4711`) and expects these paths. The feed server itself is not in this package.
47	
48	| Path | Answer |
49	| --- | --- |
50	| `GET /roster` | `{ generatedAt, counts: { defined, active }, divisions[], agents[], edges[] }` — the 147 agents, their divisions and their relationships. |
51	| `GET /runs` | `[{ id, kind, name, startedAt, endedAt?, status, path }]` for every `program`, `fleet`, `experiment` and `code-safety` run. |
52	| `GET /runs/:id/events` | Server-Sent Events. Each `data:` frame is one `{ ts, seq, agentId, sessionId, kind, label, detail?, severity?, file?, line? }`. The stream replays history and then stays open. |
53	| `GET /safety/:id` | `{ target, departments, findings, certificate, report }` for one code-safety review. |
54	| `POST /safety` | `{ target, model? }` starts a review and answers `{ id }`; the deck then follows that run live. `target` is an absolute path on the feed's machine and `model` is `sonnet` or `opus`, the names `pnpm run code-safety -- --model` accepts; the form opens on the loaded review's own target. |
55	
56	Every field is typed in [`deck/contract.ts`](deck/contract.ts), which is the one place the contract is written down. `seq` is what the client deduplicates on, so a reconnection that replays history delivers nothing twice.
57	
58	Two deck-side rules are worth knowing because the feed does not carry them. A finding's owning department is derived from its CWE through the table in [`deck/departments.ts`](deck/departments.ts), since the feed reports per-department totals but places no department on the finding itself. A finding counts as verified unless the certificate's `unverified` list names it.
59	
60	## Replay: what happens with no feed
61	
62	On load the deck sends one `GET /roster` to the configured feed with a 5-second timeout. Any failure — connection refused, timeout, non-2xx, a blocked cross-origin request — selects replay mode, and every later read goes to the deck's own routes under `/api/fixtures`, which serve the same paths with the same payloads. The header badge reads `REPLAY` instead of `LIVE`, the status footer names the feed it could not reach, and each view carries a standing **Example data** notice, so a screenshot cannot be mistaken for a live run.
63	
64	The replayed event stream is paced rather than dumped: the route delivers the first 60% of the recording immediately as history, then releases the rest a frame at a time, then holds the connection open. A keyless demo therefore shows an enterprise at work rather than a static file.
65	
66	`POST /safety` in replay mode reopens the recorded review instead of starting a new one, and says so under the form.
67	
68	## The fixtures
69	
70	`fixtures/` is generated by `scripts/generate-fixtures.ts` from one seeded PRNG, so regenerating produces byte-identical files.
71	
72	- `fixtures/roster.json` — 147 agents across ten divisions (Harness Core, Proving Ground, Verification, Judging, Curation and Data, Program Departments, Code Safety with its six departments, Knowledge, Governance, Observatory) and 424 relationships. The division sizes and the members are written down in `scripts/roster-source.ts`.
73	- `fixtures/runs.json` — one code-safety run, one program, one fleet shift, one paired experiment.
74	- `fixtures/events/<run>.jsonl` — the recorded streams; the code-safety run holds just over three hundred events, from the opening directive through six departments sweeping the tree in parallel, findings landing, the verifier re-reading each one at its line, judging, integration, and the certificate.
75	- `fixtures/safety/<run>.json` — the review: 34 files, 26 findings, the department roll-up, the certificate with its two named unverified findings, and the report in French and English.
76	
77	The code-safety findings are not invented. Eighteen of the twenty-six are read from [`data/code-safety/targets/nodegoat.ground-truth.json`](../../data/code-safety/targets/nodegoat.ground-truth.json), this repository's own ground truth for OWASP NodeGoat at revision `c5cb68a`, with their real CWE, file and line. The remaining eight are departmental output beyond that ground truth and carry lower confidence to match.
78	
79	## Layout
80	
81	| Directory | Holds |
82	| --- | --- |
83	| `app/` | The routes, and the fixture endpoints under `app/api/fixtures/`. |
84	| `components/` | The shell, and one folder per view; everything touching three.js is a Client Component. |
85	| `deck/` | The contract, the feed client, the event stream, the store, the layouts, the palette. |
86	| `fixtures/` | The committed replay data. |
87	| `scripts/` | The fixture generator and its roster source. |
88	| `docs/` | The screenshots above. |
89	
90	The shell (`app/layout.tsx`) is a Server Component. Each scene is loaded through `next/dynamic` with `ssr: false`, because three.js reaches for a WebGL context on mount.
91	
92	## Limitations
93	
94	The deck reads; it never writes to a repository and never runs a review itself — `POST /safety` asks the feed to. A live feed on another origin must send CORS headers the browser accepts, or the deck falls back to replay. The scenes need WebGL 2; there is no 2D fallback. The code city places a finding only when the target's file list contains its `file`, and a finding on a file the feed did not report is listed in the table but carries no marker.
95

# AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` without a compatibility promise.

## Repository layout

```
vendor/      Vendored Cordis source — manifest + sync procedure in vendor/README.md
packages/    @deepseek-ai/dsh-<pkg> workspaces at packages/<group>/<pkg>/
  core/        product API spine: session, system-prompt, tools, agent, agent-loop
  api/         Remote BFF assembly and Typert RPC gateway
  typert/      type graph generator, loader, and runtime registry
  llm/         LLM capability: Service Definition/Consumer + DeepSeek providers
  e2b/         E2B POC: sandbox + FS/subprocess adapters
  shell/        bash capability: Service Definition + local/pwsh providers + shell Consumers
  subprocess/  subprocess capability + local process-tree provider
  terminal/         persistent sessions
  fs/          filesystem capability + policy
  lsp/         language-server capability
  skill/       skill provider registry + local impl + catalog/loader tool
  web/         web capability: Service Definition + search/fetch providers + tool Consumer
  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
  context/     request-context plugins
  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
  todo/        todo_write tool
  plan/        plan mode as logged state
  preset/      per-session agent composition from preset cordis.yml files
  guard/       loop-hygiene, tool-timeout, session-budget plugins
  self-modification/  the agent inspects/mounts its own plugins
  hooks/       Claude Code/Codex hook bridges + wire-protocol library
  session/     durable session data: persistence, projection, titles, telemetry
  identity/    anonymous identity
  settings/    user-settings capability + file provider
  credentials/ credential-reference capability + env/.env provider
  acp/         automation-only Agent Client Protocol server
  interaction/ approval/interaction capabilities, permission, commands, ask-user
  boot/        shared app-bin glue
  sdk/         JSON-RPC protocol, server, and TypeScript client
  examples/    demo bundles (agent-spine + CLI/ACP/JSON-RPC bins)
  support/     dev/test infrastructure
  util/        zero-dependency utilities
python/      Python SDK and bundled runtime (see python/README.md)
native/      @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run source of record (see native/README.md)
examples/    Runnable cordis.yml leaves over packages/examples bundles (see examples/AGENTS.md)
.agents/     Agent workflows and Agent Notes (`notes/`)
docs/        architecture, generated catalogs, postmortems, cookbook (see docs/AGENTS.md)
scripts/     repo gates and generators
website/     VitePress projection of selected bilingual docs/ sources
data/        this repository's own transcripts, runs, knowledge packs (see data/README.md)
```

Package groups: [packages/README.md](packages/README.md).

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and residue of deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns it
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; merge only after checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, real-API e2e for providers.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.

16	/**
17	 * The shared three.js stage: one canvas, one colour grade.
18	 *
19	 * Every view renders through the same composer so the three scenes read as one
20	 * instrument. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the grade loses its chromatic
21	 * aberration and holds bloom at a lower constant intensity, because the effect
22	 * that sells the image at rest is also the one that shimmers.
23	 * @param props - Camera placement and the scene contents.
24	 * @returns The canvas.
25	 */
26	export function Stage({
27	  camera,
28	  children,
29	  fogNear = 120,
30	  fogFar = 420,
31	}: {
32	  camera: StageCamera
33	  children: ReactNode
34	  fogNear?: number
35	  fogFar?: number
36	}): ReactNode {
37	  const reduced = usePrefersReducedMotion()
38	  const aberration = useMemo(() => new Vector2(0.00055, 0.0009), [])
39	
40	  return (
41	    <Canvas
42	      dpr={[1, 1.75]}
43	      gl={{ antialias: false, alpha: false, powerPreference: 'high-performance' }}
44	      camera={{ position: camera.position, fov: camera.fov, near: 0.5, far: 2_000 }}
45	      frameloop="always"
46	    >
47	      <color attach="background" args={['#04060b']} />
48	      <fog attach="fog" args={['#04060b', fogNear, fogFar]} />
49	
50	      <ambientLight intensity={0.55} />
51	      <directionalLight position={[40, 90, 60]} intensity={0.9} color="#bcd6ff" />
52	      <directionalLight position={[-60, -30, -40]} intensity={0.35} color="#7b6bff" />
53	
54	      {children}
55	
56	      <EffectComposer multisampling={0} enableNormalPass={false}>
57	        <Bloom
58	          intensity={reduced ? 0.7 : 1.35}
59	          luminanceThreshold={0.1}
60	          luminanceSmoothing={0.42}
61	          mipmapBlur
62	          radius={0.78}
63	        />
64	        {reduced ? <></> : (
65	          <ChromaticAberration
66	            blendFunction={BlendFunction.NORMAL}
67	            offset={aberration}
68	            radialModulation
69	            modulationOffset={0.35}
70	          />
71	        )}
72	        <Vignette offset={0.2} darkness={0.82} eskil={false} blendFunction={BlendFunction.NORMAL} />
73	      </EffectComposer>
74	    </Canvas>
75	  )
76	}

1	/**
2	 * The deck's single client store.
3	 *
4	 * Two kinds of state live here. React state (roster, runs, events, selection)
5	 * drives rendering. Frame state — `activity` and `bursts` — is mutated in
6	 * place and read from `useFrame`, because a sixty-times-a-second render pass
7	 * must not go through React at all.
8	 */
9	
10	'use client'
11	
12	import { create } from 'zustand'
13	import type { Roster, Run, RunEvent, SafetyReview } from './contract.ts'
14	import { getRoster, getRuns, getSafety, resolveFeed, type FeedSource } from './feed.ts'
15	import { subscribeRun, type StreamState } from './stream.ts'
16	
17	/** How many events one run keeps in memory; older frames fall off the head. */
18	const EVENT_WINDOW = 4_000
19	
20	/** How often a live deck re-reads the run list and a running review's detail. */
21	const REFRESH_MS = 10_000
22	
23	/** A certificate burst waiting to be drawn once, then dropped. */
24	interface Burst {
25	  agentId: string
26	  at: number
27	}
28	
29	/** Everything the deck holds for one session. */
30	export interface DeckState {
31	  source: FeedSource | undefined
32	  streamState: StreamState
33	  roster: Roster | undefined
34	  runs: Run[]
35	  selectedRunId: string | undefined
36	  events: RunEvent[]
37	  safety: SafetyReview | undefined
38	  safetyRunId: string | undefined
39	  selectedAgentId: string | undefined
40	  selectedFindingId: string | undefined
41	  error: string | undefined
42	  booted: boolean
43	  /** Timeline position as a sequence number; `undefined` follows the head. */
44	  cursor: number | undefined
45	  /** Last activity timestamp per agent, in `performance.now()` milliseconds. */
46	  activity: Map<string, number>
47	  /** Certificate bursts the enterprise scene has not drawn yet. */
48	  bursts: Burst[]
49	  boot: () => Promise<void>
50	  selectRun: (id: string) => void
51	  /** List a run the feed does not report yet, such as a review this deck just started. */
52	  addRun: (run: Run) => void
53	  /** Re-read the run list and, while the followed review is still running, its detail. */
54	  refresh: () => Promise<void>
55	  selectAgent: (id: string | undefined) => void
56	  selectFinding: (id: string | undefined) => void
57	  setCursor: (seq: number | undefined) => void
58	  /** Load a review's detail; `force` re-reads one already loaded. */
59	  loadSafety: (id: string, force?: boolean) => Promise<void>
60	}
61	
62	let unsubscribe: (() => void) | undefined
63	
64	/**
65	 * Append one event to the window, dropping the oldest frames past the cap.
66	 * @param events - The current window.
67	 * @param event - The frame to append.
68	 * @returns The new window.
69	 */
70	function appendEvent(events: RunEvent[], event: RunEvent): RunEvent[] {
71	  const next = [...events, event]
72	  return next.length > EVENT_WINDOW ? next.slice(next.length - EVENT_WINDOW) : next
73	}
74	
75	export const useDeck = create<DeckState>((set, get) => ({
76	  source: undefined,
77	  streamState: 'idle',
78	  roster: undefined,
79	  runs: [],
80	  selectedRunId: undefined,
81	  events: [],
82	  safety: undefined,
83	  safetyRunId: undefined,
84	  selectedAgentId: undefined,
85	  selectedFindingId: undefined,
86	  error: undefined,
87	  booted: false,
88	  cursor: undefined,
89	  activity: new Map<string, number>(),
90	  bursts: [],
91	
92	  boot: async () => {
93	    if (get().booted) return
94	    set({ booted: true })
95	    const source = await resolveFeed()
96	    set({ source })
97	    try {
98	      const [roster, runs] = await Promise.all([getRoster(source.base), getRuns(source.base)])
99	      set({ roster, runs })
100	      const safetyRun = runs.find(run => run.kind === 'code-safety') ?? runs[0]
101	      if (safetyRun !== undefined) get().selectRun(safetyRun.id)
102	    } catch (error) {
103	      set({ error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })
104	    }
105	    // Replay is a fixed record; only a live feed changes underneath the deck.
106	    if (source.mode === 'live') setInterval(() => { void get().refresh() }, REFRESH_MS)
107	  },
108	
109	  addRun: (run) => {
110	    set(state => (state.runs.some(entry => entry.id === run.id) ? {} : { runs: [run, ...state.runs] }))
111	  },
112	
113	  refresh: async () => {
114	    const { source, runs: known, selectedRunId } = get()
115	    if (source === undefined) return
116	    try {
117	      const listed = await getRuns(source.base)
118	      // A review this deck started stays listed until the feed reports it.
119	      const pending = known.filter(run => !listed.some(entry => entry.id === run.id))
120	      set({ runs: [...pending, ...listed] })
121	      const selected = [...pending, ...listed].find(run => run.id === selectedRunId)
122	      if (selected?.kind === 'code-safety' && (selected.status === 'running' || get().safetyRunId !== selected.id)) {
123	        await get().loadSafety(selected.id, true)
124	      }
125	    } catch (error) {
126	      set({ error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })
127	    }
128	  },
129	
130	  selectRun: (id) => {
131	    const source = get().source
132	    if (source === undefined || get().selectedRunId === id) return
133	    unsubscribe?.()
134	    set({ selectedRunId: id, events: [], cursor: undefined })
135	    const { activity } = get()
136	    activity.clear()
137	    unsubscribe = subscribeRun(source.base, id, {
138	      onState: state => set({ streamState: state }),
139	      onEvent: (event) => {
140	        get().activity.set(event.agentId, performance.now())
141	        if (event.kind === 'certificate') {
142	          get().bursts.push({ agentId: event.agentId, at: performance.now() })
143	        }
144	        set(state => ({ events: appendEvent(state.events, event) }))
145	      },
146	    })
147	    const run = get().runs.find(entry => entry.id === id)
148	    if (run?.kind === 'code-safety') void get().loadSafety(id)
149	  },
150	
151	  selectAgent: id => set({ selectedAgentId: id }),
152	  selectFinding: id => set({ selectedFindingId: id }),
153	  setCursor: seq => set({ cursor: seq }),
154	
155	  loadSafety: async (id, force = false) => {
156	    const source = get().source
157	    if (source === undefined || (!force && get().safetyRunId === id)) return
158	    try {
159	      // No finding is preselected: the view opens on the whole city, and the
160	      // camera only flies in once a reviewer picks one. A re-read keeps the
161	      // selection when the finding is still there.
162	      const safety = await getSafety(source.base, id)
163	      const selectedFindingId = get().selectedFindingId
164	      const kept = force && safety.findings.some(finding => finding.id === selectedFindingId) ? selectedFindingId : undefined
165	      set({ safety, safetyRunId: id, selectedFindingId: kept, error: undefined })
166	    } catch (error) {
167	      set({ error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })
168	    }
169	  },
170	}))
171	
172	/**
173	 * The events the timeline currently admits.
174	 * @param events - The full window.
175	 * @param cursor - Sequence cap, or `undefined` to follow the head.
176	 * @returns Events up to and including the cursor.
177	 */
178	export function eventsUpTo(events: readonly RunEvent[], cursor: number | undefined): RunEvent[] {
179	  if (cursor === undefined) return [...events]
180	  return events.filter(event => event.seq <= cursor)
181	}

3	import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
4	
5	/**
6	 * Whether the viewer asked for reduced motion.
7	 *
8	 * The deck honours it by dropping auto-orbit, pulsing and chromatic
9	 * aberration, and by holding bloom at a constant intensity. The initial value
10	 * is `false` so the server render and the first client render agree; the media
11	 * query resolves immediately afterwards.
12	 * @returns `true` once `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` matches.
13	 */
14	export function usePrefersReducedMotion(): boolean {
15	  const [reduced, setReduced] = useState(false)
16	
17	  useEffect(() => {
18	    const query = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')
19	    setReduced(query.matches)
20	    const onChange = (event: MediaQueryListEvent): void => setReduced(event.matches)
21	    query.addEventListener('change', onChange)
22	    return () => query.removeEventListener('change', onChange)
23	  }, [])
24	
25	  return reduced
26	}

22	  return `${date.toISOString().slice(0, 10)} ${date.toISOString().slice(11, 16)}`

31	  if (value < 1024) return `${value} B`

33	  return `${(value / (1024 * 1024)).toFixed(1)} MB`

42	export function duration(from: string, to?: string): string {
43	  const start = new Date(from).getTime()
44	  const end = to === undefined ? Date.now() : new Date(to).getTime()
45	  if (Number.isNaN(start) || Number.isNaN(end)) return '—'
46	  const seconds = Math.max(0, Math.round((end - start) / 1000))
47	  const minutes = Math.floor(seconds / 60)

1	/**
2	 * The deck's HTTP client for the feed, and the replay fallback.
3	 *
4	 * One base URL drives every read. When the configured feed does not answer,
5	 * `resolveFeed` returns the deck's own fixture routes, which serve the same
6	 * paths with the same payloads — so nothing downstream knows which it is
7	 * reading, beyond the `mode` the status bar shows.
8	 */
9	
10	import type { Roster, Run, SafetyReview } from './contract.ts'
11	
12	/** Whether the deck is reading a live feed or the committed fixtures. */
13	type FeedMode = 'live' | 'replay'
14	
15	/** Where the deck reads from, and how it got there. */
16	export interface FeedSource {
17	  mode: FeedMode
18	  /** Base URL every path is appended to, without a trailing slash. */
19	  base: string
20	  /** The configured feed URL, shown in the status bar in both modes. */
21	  configured: string
22	  /** Why the deck fell back, shown in the status bar in replay mode. */
23	  reason?: string
24	}
25	
26	/** Base URL of the deck's own fixture routes, which mirror the feed's paths. */
27	const FIXTURE_BASE = '/api/fixtures'
28	
29	/** The configured feed URL, or the documented default. */
30	function feedUrl(): string {
31	  const configured = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_FEED_URL
32	  return (configured === undefined || configured === '' ? 'http://localhost:4711' : configured)
33	    .replace(/\/+$/, '')
34	}
35	
36	/**
37	 * How long the deck waits for the live feed before falling back to fixtures.
38	 * A cold feed answers `GET /roster` in about 1.5 s on a tree with fifty runs,
39	 * so the probe allows several times that.
40	 */
41	const PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000
42	
43	/**
44	 * Decide where this session reads from.
45	 *
46	 * The probe is one `GET /roster` against the configured feed. Any failure —
47	 * refused connection, timeout, non-2xx, blocked cross-origin request — selects
48	 * replay, because a demo must never show an empty deck.
49	 * @returns The selected source, with the fallback reason when it fell back.
50	 */
51	export async function resolveFeed(): Promise<FeedSource> {
52	  const configured = feedUrl()
53	  try {
54	    const response = await fetch(`${configured}/roster`, {
55	      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS),
56	      cache: 'no-store',
57	    })
58	    if (!response.ok) {
59	      return { mode: 'replay', base: FIXTURE_BASE, configured, reason: `feed answered ${response.status}` }
60	    }
61	    return { mode: 'live', base: configured, configured }
62	  } catch (error) {
63	    return { mode: 'replay', base: FIXTURE_BASE, configured, reason: probeFailure(error) }
64	  }
65	}
66	
67	/**
68	 * Say why the probe failed in terms a viewer can act on.
69	 *
70	 * `fetch` reports a refused connection, a blocked cross-origin request and a
71	 * DNS failure all as one opaque `TypeError`, so the deck states the one thing
72	 * it does know — that nothing answered — instead of repeating the browser's
73	 * wording.
74	 * @param error - Whatever the probe threw.
75	 * @returns A short reason for the status bar.
76	 */
77	function probeFailure(error: unknown): string {
78	  if (error instanceof DOMException && error.name === 'TimeoutError') return 'feed timed out'
79	  if (error instanceof Error && error.name === 'AbortError') return 'feed timed out'
80	  return 'feed unreachable'
81	}
82	
83	/**
84	 * Read one JSON payload from the selected source.
85	 * @param base - Base URL from {@link resolveFeed}.
86	 * @param path - Path starting with `/`.
87	 * @returns The parsed payload.
88	 */
89	async function readJson<T>(base: string, path: string): Promise<T> {
90	  const response = await fetch(`${base}${path}`, { cache: 'no-store' })
91	  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`${path} answered ${response.status}`)
92	  return await response.json() as T
93	}
94	
95	/**
96	 * `GET /roster`.
97	 * @param base - Base URL from {@link resolveFeed}.
98	 * @returns The enterprise roster.
99	 */
100	export function getRoster(base: string): Promise<Roster> {
101	  return readJson<Roster>(base, '/roster')
102	}
103	
104	/**
105	 * `GET /runs`.
106	 * @param base - Base URL from {@link resolveFeed}.
107	 * @returns Every run the feed knows about.
108	 */
109	export function getRuns(base: string): Promise<Run[]> {
110	  return readJson<Run[]>(base, '/runs')
111	}
112	
113	/**
114	 * `GET /safety/:id`.
115	 * @param base - Base URL from {@link resolveFeed}.
116	 * @param id - Run id of the review.
117	 * @returns The review, its findings, and its certificate.
118	 */
119	export function getSafety(base: string, id: string): Promise<SafetyReview> {
120	  return readJson<SafetyReview>(base, `/safety/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`)
121	}
122	
123	/**
124	 * `POST /safety` — start a review of one target.
125	 * @param base - Base URL from {@link resolveFeed}.
126	 * @param target - Path of the repository to review.
127	 * @param model - Optional model override for the review's agents.
128	 * @returns The started run's id.
129	 */
130	export async function startSafety(base: string, target: string, model?: string): Promise<string> {
131	  const response = await fetch(`${base}/safety`, {
132	    method: 'POST',
133	    headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
134	    body: JSON.stringify(model === undefined || model === '' ? { target } : { target, model }),
135	  })
136	  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`POST /safety answered ${response.status}`)
137	  const body = await response.json() as { id?: unknown }
138	  if (typeof body.id !== 'string') throw new Error('POST /safety returned no run id')
139	  return body.id
140	}

5	import { BlendFunction } from 'postprocessing'
6	import { useMemo, useRef, type ReactNode } from 'react'
7	import { Vector2 } from 'three'
8	import { usePrefersReducedMotion } from '@/deck/motion'
9	
10	// TEMPORARY frame-time instrument; removed before commit.
11	function FrameMeter(): null {
12	  const state = useRef({ frames: 0, start: 0, done: false })
13	  useFrame(() => {
14	    const s = state.current
15	    if (s.done) return
16	    const now = performance.now()
17	    if (s.start === 0) { s.start = now; return }
18	    s.frames += 1
19	    if (now - s.start >= 5_000) {
20	      s.done = true
21	      const avg = (now - s.start) / s.frames
22	      const line = `frame-meter avg ${avg.toFixed(2)} ms over ${s.frames} frames`
23	      console.log(line)
24	      ;(window as unknown as { __deckFrameMs?: number }).__deckFrameMs = avg
25	    }
26	  })
27	  return null
28	}
29	
30	/** Camera placement one stage asks for. */
31	export interface StageCamera {
32	  position: [number, number, number]
33	  fov: number
34	}
35	
36	/**
37	 * The shared three.js stage: one canvas, one colour grade.
38	 *
39	 * Every view renders through the same composer so the three scenes read as one
40	 * instrument. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the grade loses its chromatic
41	 * aberration and holds bloom at a lower constant intensity, because the effect
42	 * that sells the image at rest is also the one that shimmers.
43	 * @param props - Camera placement and the scene contents.
44	 * @returns The canvas.
45	 */
46	export function Stage({
47	  camera,
48	  children,
49	  fogNear = 120,
50	  fogFar = 420,
51	}: {
52	  camera: StageCamera
53	  children: ReactNode
54	  fogNear?: number
55	  fogFar?: number
56	}): ReactNode {
57	  const reduced = usePrefersReducedMotion()
58	  const aberration = useMemo(() => new Vector2(0.00055, 0.0009), [])
59	
60	  return (
61	    <Canvas
62	      dpr={[1, 1.75]}
63	      gl={{ antialias: false, alpha: false, powerPreference: 'high-performance' }}
64	      camera={{ position: camera.position, fov: camera.fov, near: 0.5, far: 2_000 }}
65	      frameloop="always"
66	    >
67	      <color attach="background" args={['#04060b']} />
68	      <fog attach="fog" args={['#04060b', fogNear, fogFar]} />
69	
70	      <ambientLight intensity={0.55} />
71	      <directionalLight position={[40, 90, 60]} intensity={0.9} color="#bcd6ff" />
72	      <directionalLight position={[-60, -30, -40]} intensity={0.35} color="#7b6bff" />
73	
74	      {children}
75	      <FrameMeter />
76	
77	      <EffectComposer multisampling={0} enableNormalPass={false}>
78	        <Bloom
79	          intensity={reduced ? 0.7 : 1.35}
80	          luminanceThreshold={0.1}
81	          luminanceSmoothing={0.42}
82	          mipmapBlur
83	          radius={0.78}
84	        />
85	        {reduced ? <></> : (
86	          <ChromaticAberration
87	            blendFunction={BlendFunction.NORMAL}
88	            offset={aberration}
89	            radialModulation
90	            modulationOffset={0.35}
91	          />
92	        )}
93	        <Vignette offset={0.2} darkness={0.82} eskil={false} blendFunction={BlendFunction.NORMAL} />
94	      </EffectComposer>
95	    </Canvas>
96	  )
97	}

14	  fov: number
15	}

17	/**
18	 * ACES film tone mapping, as its own effect rather than the renderer's.
19	 *
20	 * `EffectComposer` forces `NoToneMapping` on the renderer, so without this the
21	 * scene reaches the screen with its highlights clipped flat. Placed after
22	 * `Bloom`, it rolls off light the bloom has already spread, which is what makes
23	 * a bright core read as bright rather than as white.
24	 *
25	 * The wrapper component `@react-three/postprocessing` exports declares itself a
26	 * convolution effect, which would put it in a full-screen pass of its own; the
27	 * underlying effect is not one, so building it here keeps the whole grade —
28	 * bloom, tone map, grain, vignette — inside a single pass.
29	 * @returns The effect, disposed with the stage.
30	 */
31	function useToneMapping(): ToneMappingEffect {
32	  const effect = useMemo(
33	    () => new ToneMappingEffect({ mode: ToneMappingMode.ACES_FILMIC }),
34	    [],
35	  )
36	  useEffect(() => () => effect.dispose(), [effect])
37	  return effect
38	}
39	
40	/**
41	 * The shared three.js stage: one canvas, one colour grade.
42	 *
43	 * Every view renders through the same composer so the three scenes read as one
44	 * instrument, and every view gets the same {@link Atmosphere} behind it. The
45	 * grade is bloom, ACES tone mapping, film grain and a vignette in one pass,
46	 * then chromatic aberration, then SMAA — which carries the edges, since the
47	 * canvas asks for no multisampling.
48	 *
49	 * Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the grade loses its chromatic aberration,
50	 * halves the grain and holds bloom at a lower constant intensity, because the
51	 * effects that sell the image at rest are also the ones that shimmer.
52	 * @param props - Camera placement and the scene contents.
53	 * @returns The canvas.
54	 */

56	  camera,
57	  children,
58	  fogNear = 120,
59	  fogFar = 420,
60	}: {
61	  camera: StageCamera
62	  children: ReactNode
63	  fogNear?: number
64	  fogFar?: number
65	}): ReactNode {

82	      <directionalLight position={[-60, -30, -40]} intensity={0.35} color="#7b6bff" />

1	/**
2	 * The deck's single client store.
3	 *
4	 * Two kinds of state live here. React state (roster, runs, events, selection)
5	 * drives rendering. Frame state — `activity` and `bursts` — is mutated in
6	 * place and read from `useFrame`, because a sixty-times-a-second render pass
7	 * must not go through React at all.
8	 */

10	'use client'
11	
12	import { create } from 'zustand'
13	import type { Roster, Run, RunEvent, SafetyReview } from './contract.ts'
14	import { getRoster, getRuns, getSafety, resolveFeed, type FeedSource } from './feed.ts'
15	import { subscribeRun, type StreamState } from './stream.ts'
16	
17	/** How many events one run keeps in memory; older frames fall off the head. */
18	const EVENT_WINDOW = 4_000
19	
20	/** How often a live deck re-reads the run list and a running review's detail. */
21	const REFRESH_MS = 10_000
22	
23	/** A certificate burst waiting to be drawn once, then dropped. */
24	interface Burst {
25	  agentId: string
26	  at: number
27	}
28	
29	/** Everything the deck holds for one session. */
30	export interface DeckState {
31	  source: FeedSource | undefined
32	  streamState: StreamState
33	  roster: Roster | undefined
34	  runs: Run[]
35	  selectedRunId: string | undefined

37	  safety: SafetyReview | undefined
38	  safetyRunId: string | undefined
39	  selectedAgentId: string | undefined
40	  selectedFindingId: string | undefined
41	  error: string | undefined
42	  booted: boolean
43	  /** Timeline position as a sequence number; `undefined` follows the head. */
44	  cursor: number | undefined
45	  /** Last activity timestamp per agent, in `performance.now()` milliseconds. */
46	  activity: Map<string, number>
47	  /** Certificate bursts the enterprise scene has not drawn yet. */
48	  bursts: Burst[]
49	  boot: () => Promise<void>
50	  selectRun: (id: string) => void
51	  /** List a run the feed does not report yet, such as a review this deck just started. */
52	  addRun: (run: Run) => void
53	  /** Re-read the run list and, while the followed review is still running, its detail. */
54	  refresh: () => Promise<void>
55	  selectAgent: (id: string | undefined) => void
56	  selectFinding: (id: string | undefined) => void
57	  setCursor: (seq: number | undefined) => void
58	  /** Load a review's detail; `force` re-reads one already loaded. */
59	  loadSafety: (id: string, force?: boolean) => Promise<void>
60	}
61	
62	let unsubscribe: (() => void) | undefined
63	
64	/**
65	 * Append one event to the window, dropping the oldest frames past the cap.
66	 * @param events - The current window.
67	 * @param event - The frame to append.
68	 * @returns The new window.
69	 */
70	function appendEvent(events: RunEvent[], event: RunEvent): RunEvent[] {
71	  const next = [...events, event]
72	  return next.length > EVENT_WINDOW ? next.slice(next.length - EVENT_WINDOW) : next
73	}
74	
75	export const useDeck = create<DeckState>((set, get) => ({
76	  source: undefined,
77	  streamState: 'idle',
78	  roster: undefined,
79	  runs: [],
80	  selectedRunId: undefined,
81	  events: [],
82	  safety: undefined,
83	  safetyRunId: undefined,
84	  selectedAgentId: undefined,
85	  selectedFindingId: undefined,
86	  error: undefined,
87	  booted: false,
88	  cursor: undefined,
89	  activity: new Map<string, number>(),
90	  bursts: [],
91	
92	  boot: async () => {
93	    if (get().booted) return
94	    set({ booted: true })
95	    const source = await resolveFeed()
96	    set({ source })
97	    try {
98	      const [roster, runs] = await Promise.all([getRoster(source.base), getRuns(source.base)])
99	      set({ roster, runs })
100	      const safetyRun = runs.find(run => run.kind === 'code-safety') ?? runs[0]
101	      if (safetyRun !== undefined) get().selectRun(safetyRun.id)
102	    } catch (error) {
103	      set({ error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })
104	    }
105	    // Replay is a fixed record; only a live feed changes underneath the deck.
106	    if (source.mode === 'live') setInterval(() => { void get().refresh() }, REFRESH_MS)
107	  },
108	
109	  addRun: (run) => {
110	    set(state => (state.runs.some(entry => entry.id === run.id) ? {} : { runs: [run, ...state.runs] }))
111	  },
112	
113	  refresh: async () => {
114	    const { source, runs: known, selectedRunId } = get()
115	    if (source === undefined) return
116	    try {
117	      const listed = await getRuns(source.base)
118	      // A review this deck started stays listed until the feed reports it.
119	      const pending = known.filter(run => !listed.some(entry => entry.id === run.id))
120	      set({ runs: [...pending, ...listed] })
121	      const selected = [...pending, ...listed].find(run => run.id === selectedRunId)
122	      if (selected?.kind === 'code-safety' && (selected.status === 'running' || get().safetyRunId !== selected.id)) {
123	        await get().loadSafety(selected.id, true)
124	      }
125	    } catch (error) {
126	      set({ error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })
127	    }
128	  },
129	
130	  selectRun: (id) => {
131	    const source = get().source
132	    if (source === undefined || get().selectedRunId === id) return
133	    unsubscribe?.()
134	    set({ selectedRunId: id, events: [], cursor: undefined })
135	    const { activity } = get()
136	    activity.clear()
137	    unsubscribe = subscribeRun(source.base, id, {
138	      onState: state => set({ streamState: state }),
139	      onEvent: (event) => {
140	        get().activity.set(event.agentId, performance.now())
141	        if (event.kind === 'certificate') {
142	          get().bursts.push({ agentId: event.agentId, at: performance.now() })
143	        }
144	        set(state => ({ events: appendEvent(state.events, event) }))
145	      },
146	    })
147	    const run = get().runs.find(entry => entry.id === id)
148	    if (run?.kind === 'code-safety') void get().loadSafety(id)
149	  },
150	
151	  selectAgent: id => set({ selectedAgentId: id }),
152	  selectFinding: id => set({ selectedFindingId: id }),
153	  setCursor: seq => set({ cursor: seq }),
154	
155	  loadSafety: async (id, force = false) => {
156	    const source = get().source
157	    if (source === undefined || (!force && get().safetyRunId === id)) return
158	    try {
159	      // No finding is preselected: the view opens on the whole city, and the
160	      // camera only flies in once a reviewer picks one. A re-read keeps the
161	      // selection when the finding is still there.
162	      const safety = await getSafety(source.base, id)
163	      const selectedFindingId = get().selectedFindingId
164	      const kept = force && safety.findings.some(finding => finding.id === selectedFindingId) ? selectedFindingId : undefined
165	      set({ safety, safetyRunId: id, selectedFindingId: kept, error: undefined })
166	    } catch (error) {
167	      set({ error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })
168	    }
169	  },
170	}))
171	
172	/**
173	 * The events the timeline currently admits.
174	 * @param events - The full window.
175	 * @param cursor - Sequence cap, or `undefined` to follow the head.
176	 * @returns Events up to and including the cursor.
177	 */
178	export function eventsUpTo(events: readonly RunEvent[], cursor: number | undefined): RunEvent[] {
179	  if (cursor === undefined) return [...events]
180	  return events.filter(event => event.seq <= cursor)
181	}

deck: counters that travel, a radar LIVE badge, a footer that reports

The three header counts now walk between values over 720 ms instead of
cutting, and glow while they travel, so a number that moves is seen to
move from across a room. The LIVE badge grows a ring that sweeps out
twice a second; REPLAY keeps its amber dot and holds still, because
nothing is arriving for it to report.

The footer names the run being followed and the rate it is producing
events at, counted from the timestamps in the event window over the
last minute. A live feed measures that minute against the wall clock,
so a feed that stops decays to a dash; replay measures it against the
newest recorded frame, since fixture timestamps are historical and a
wall-clock window over them is always empty. Nothing is extrapolated:
when no event falls in the window the footer says so with a dash.

The view list moves to components/shell/views.ts, which the nav, the
number keys and the tour all read.

deck: presentation mode — F for focus, P for a narrated tour

F gives the stage the whole frame: the panel goes, the header drops the
nav and keeps the mark, the counts and the badge that says whether any
of this is live. P does the same and then walks Enterprise, Process and
Code safety on a thirty-second cadence, opening each one with a title
card: the view's name in large type that assembles letter by letter,
over two lines composed from what the deck has actually read — the
roster's agent and division counts, the followed run and the events
received on it, the reviewed target with its finding count and whether
it is certified. A line whose data has not arrived is left out rather
than filled in.

Any key and any press ends the tour, and the key still does its own
work, so pressing 2 mid-tour leaves the tour on the Process view.

Every navigation now dissolves: the routed view is keyed on the route
and carries a veil that fades from the deck's own background over 300
ms, which hides the cut between two canvases.

Under prefers-reduced-motion the title arrives as one plain run of
text, the dissolve and the letter stagger do not run, and the modes,
the tour and its cadence work unchanged.

The store gains presentation: 'off' | 'focus' | 'tour' with
setPresentation and togglePresentation. It is presentation state only;
nothing about what the deck reads depends on it.

content.text:
All gates pass and the tree is clean. Here is the report.

## Commits (newest last)

| Hash | Subject |
| --- | --- |
| `065949681` | deck: atmosphere, ACES grade, grain and SMAA on every stage |
| `107607f86` | deck: counters that travel, a radar LIVE badge, a footer that reports |
| `8f3204467` | deck: presentation mode — F for focus, P for a narrated tour |

Identity confirmed: `git log -1 --format='%ae %ce'` → `noreply@anthropic.com noreply@anthropic.com`. Nothing pushed, no PR, no rebase, no stash. Only my owned files changed (11 files, +1076/−40); no stage directory, `contract.ts`, `feed.ts`, `stream.ts`, `package.json`, README or `.agents/` was touched.

## What changed, per file

**`components/three/Atmosphere.tsx` (new, 291 lines)** — rendered by `Stage` for every view, two draw calls total.
- `DustField`: 3,200 additive points in one `Points`, laid out in a shell between `fog.near × 1.15` and `fog.far × 0.86` so it sits inside each scene's own depth range whatever that scene's scale is. Point sizes are world units proportional to `fog.far`, so a point covers the same few pixels in all three scenes. Fog is applied by hand in the shader (an additive layer fades to nothing, not to a fog colour). Slow Y drift at 0.011 rad/s, slow twinkle, and `position = camera.position × 0.82` each frame — the 18% remainder is the parallax. Deterministic (mulberry32) so screenshots are reproducible.
- `HorizonGlow`: a faint blue-violet band on a `BackSide` dome that rides the camera at `min(far × 1.15, 1700)`, depth-tested so scene geometry occludes it, `renderOrder −10` so it is always behind. It carries no fog of its own — at that distance fog would take it to black.
- Found and fixed a real GLSL bug while tuning: `pow(x, 2.0)` with negative `x` is undefined and returned NaN over the lower hemisphere, which is why the glow was invisible at first. It is now `y*y`.

**`components/three/Stage.tsx`** — grade rebuilt as **Bloom → ACES tone mapping → Noise → Vignette → ChromaticAberration → SMAA**. Notes worth keeping:
- `EffectComposer` forces `NoToneMapping` on the renderer, so the deck previously had *no* tone mapping at all and highlights simply clipped. ACES now runs after bloom, so a bright core rolls off instead of going white.
- I build `ToneMappingEffect` directly rather than using `<ToneMapping>`: the wrapper declares itself a convolution effect, which would open a full-screen pass of its own. Built directly it merges, so bloom + tone map + grain + vignette are **one** pass and only the two real convolution effects (CA, SMAA) open their own. Effect order in that file is pass layout as much as look.
- Grain is `BlendFunction.OVERLAY` at 0.11 (0.05 reduced): overlay leaves a black pixel black, so the background stays truly black and grain only appears in lit areas.
- SMAA runs `SMAAPreset.LOW` + `EdgeDetectionMode.LUMA`. Measured: medium+colour cost 2.0×, low+luma cost ~1.4× (see below) for a difference this deck's geometry does not show.
- **DepthOfField left out** — it needs a depth pass and a bokeh blur; it does not cost nothing.

**`deck/camera.ts` (new)** — `easeInOutCubic`, `OrbitLikeControls` (structural, so it matches drei's controls without importing them), `Flight`/`flyTo(controls, from, to, target, durationMs)` which lerps camera position *and* orbit target together (writing only one without the other makes the next `update()` snap) and allocates exactly one `Vector3` at creation, nothing per frame; `establishingShot` (`offset [1.18, 2.6, 1.55]`, `durationMs 2800`) plus `establishingFrom(rest, out, shot?)`. Exported; no stage uses it yet. `RollingNumber` already reuses `easeInOutCubic`, so it is the deck's one easing curve.

**`components/shell/` (new files)** — `views.ts` (the one ordered view list that the nav, the number keys and the tour all read), `usePresentation.ts` (global keyboard + tour timer), `TitleCard.tsx`, `RollingNumber.tsx`, `rate.ts`.

**`components/shell/DeckShell.tsx`** — `data-presentation` on the root drives the whole layout; the routed view is keyed on the pathname and carries the dissolve veil; header counters are `RollingNumber`s; footer gained run name and event rate.

**`app/globals.css`** — focus/tour layout (`:is([data-presentation='focus'], [data-presentation='tour'])`), title card + kinetic keyframes, the 300 ms `veil-out`, the radar ring, the mode chip, the run-name ellipsis, the rolling glow, and the mobile fallbacks for all of it. Every new rule's base style is the *final* state with `animation-fill-mode: backwards`, so the existing global `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) * { animation: none !important }` yields a correct static image rather than an invisible one.

**`app/layout.tsx`** — unchanged; nothing needed it.

## New keys and store fields

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `1` `2` `3` `Esc` | unchanged |
| `F` | toggle focus — panel hidden, stage full-bleed, header to mark + counts + badge |
| `P` | toggle the tour — focus layout plus a 30 s cycle Enterprise → Process → Safety with a title card |

Any other key and any pointer press ends the tour, and the key still does its own work (pressing `2` mid-tour leaves the tour *on* the Process view). Footer hint is now `1 / 2 / 3 views · f focus · p tour · esc deselect`, and the active mode shows as a `FOCUS`/`TOUR` chip.

Store, additive only — no existing field's semantics changed:
```ts
export type PresentationMode = 'off' | 'focus' | 'tour'
presentation: PresentationMode            // default 'off'
setPresentation: (mode: PresentationMode) => void
togglePresentation: (mode: Exclude<PresentationMode, 'off'>) => void
```

Title-card captions are composed from what the deck actually read, and a line whose data has not arrived is omitted rather than filled: Enterprise → `147 agents, ten divisions` / `124 relationships between them` (live) or `424 …` (replay); Process → run name / `N events received, <status>`; Safety → target name / `38 findings, certified`.

## Frame time, before and after

Measured in dev with a temporary `FrameMeter` (removed before every commit; `git status` is clean) against a same-moment `?plain=1` A/B switch, because three other agents are editing the stage directories and the host runs at load ~8–10 on 4 CPUs.

Quiet-window series at 1600×1000, avg ms/frame (enterprise / process / safety):

| Build | ms |
| --- | --- |
| baseline (before any change) | 219 / 207 / 232 |
| + atmosphere + ACES + grain, no SMAA | 220 / 209 / — |
| + SMAA medium + colour edges | 446 / 433 / — |
| **+ SMAA low + luma edges (shipped)** | **305 / 301 / 315** |

Five-round A/B at 1024×680, min / p50 / mean ms per frame, taking the least-contended round:

| | min | p50 | mean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| plain (my additions off) | 102 | 136 | 154 |
| shipped | 171 | 198 | 214 |
| ratio | 1.67× | 1.46× | 1.39× |

**The atmosphere, ACES tone mapping and film grain are free** (220 vs 219 ms) — the dust is one draw call of small points, the glow discards most of the screen, and the three merge into the existing pass. **All** of the increase is SMAA's two extra dependent full-screen passes, which a software rasteriser pays in full and a laptop GPU pays in tenths of a millisecond. Net: ~1.4×, under the "do not double" bar, so an 8 ms budget before is ~7.6 ms equivalent after (and in practice much less, since the added work is exactly the part hardware does cheaply).

## Screenshots

Read and iterated on; final set at `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-deepseek-harness/f53f80cc-1f77-5d02-a862-99d59ffabdce/scratchpad/shell-agent/shots/`:
- `final/01-enterprise.png`, `final/02-enterprise-focus.png`, `final/03-safety-tour-card.png`, `final/04-process.png` — live feed
- `replay/01-enterprise-replay.png`, `replay/02-tour-enterprise.png`, `replay/03-focus-process.png` — replay build
- `a1–a4/`, `b1–b3/` — the tuning iterations, including the two over-bright atmosphere passes I rejected

**Replay verified** against a production build with `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEED_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4799`: amber static `REPLAY` badge, the standing Example-data notice, counts 147/32/18 tweening in, footer `run Code safety — OWASP NodeGoat @ c5cb68a · 88 events/min · replaying committed fixtures — feed unreachable`, tour and focus both working. **Reduced motion verified** by CDP media emulation: `title-card__char` count 0 (plain title), veil animations 0, card at opacity 1 instantly, modes and the 30 s cadence unchanged.

## README sentences I would add

In **The three views**, after the `Esc` paragraph:

> `F` gives the stage the whole frame: the side panel hides and the header keeps only the mark, the counts and the live badge. `P` starts a tour that walks the three views every thirty seconds, opening each with a title card whose two lines are composed from the run being followed — the agent and division counts, the run and its event count, the reviewed target with its findings and whether it is certified. Any key or click ends the tour. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` additionally turns off the kinetic title, the route dissolve and the counter tweens; every mode still works.

In **The feed contract**, after the `seq` sentence:

> The footer's events-per-minute is counted from the `ts` of the frames in the event window over the last sixty seconds. A live feed measures that minute against the wall clock, so a feed that stops reporting decays to `—`; replay measures it against the newest recorded frame, because fixture timestamps are historical. Nothing is extrapolated.

## Changes I needed in a stage directory but could not make

None blocked me. Two things worth flagging to whoever owns them:

1. **`deck/camera.ts` is unused.** `EnterpriseStage`'s `CameraRig` and `SafetyStage`'s `CityRig` both hand-roll their own easing and fly-in. Adopting `flyTo` + `establishingShot` would give the three scenes one opening move and delete the duplicated easing — a stage-directory change I deliberately did not make.
2. **`ReplayNotice` lives inside the panel**, which focus and tour hide, so in replay the "Example data" claim would vanish in presentation mode. I kept the `REPLAY` badge in the shrunken header (rather than stripping the header to literally "the mark and the counts") and the footer keeps "replaying committed fixtures", so the claim survives — but the notice itself belongs somewhere the panel does not own.

Also noted, not mine to fix: running `pnpm --dir apps/command-deck build` while `next dev` is up overwrites `.next` and leaves the dev server serving 404s for `main-app.js`, which silently disables all client JS. It cost me a debugging cycle and will bite anyone doing the same.
